compromise.summary: One apprenticeship scheme for every trade: each apprentice learns inside a firm under published terms and a standard test, with public funds paying for school places and for places that firms cannot offer alone. Entry is open and fee-free, and any levy on employers comes with guaranteed places.
compromise.details: Keeps: Social market economy's employer-run training with state-paid schools, from Germany's dual vocational training system; Guild economy's regulated training and quality standards, set under each trade's statutes (inferred); Keynesian welfare capitalism's training places that expand in slumps (inferred). Blocks: Guild economy's entry fees and approval by existing masters, blocked by fee-free entry and a published test open to all; Social market economy's employer levy, blocked by guaranteed places and a review of starts before any new levy; Feudalism's labour services crowding out learning, blocked by protected training hours in every contract. Test: starts by trade, level and firm size, and completion, measured yearly for five years against the three years before the change. Source: BIBB, Dual vocational education and training pays off (GOVET presentation); University of Konstanz study on apprenticeship costs and profits; Boileau, Le Livre des métiers (c. 1268); Resolution Foundation, Trading up or trading off (2019); Beveridge, Social Insurance and Allied Services (1942); Bloch, Feudal Society (1939-1940).
